text:
sam: Heads up — eu-west-1 dedicated slice (slice-dedicated-45) 99p latency jumped from ~120ms -> ~2.1s at ~09:32 UTC. Customers reported timeouts. Saw a big egress queue spike and NVMe io bursts in the host logs. Putting this here so ops can coordinate.
maria: seeing same. shelf-17 NIC counters show Tx bursts, and kvcache regen for a handful of tenants. Likely a noisy tenant doing heavy mlprep + batched uploads. Can we route offending traffic off the slice to a warm reserve? Cost tradeoff but faster mitigation.
aj: quick mitigation idea: fall back a fraction of requests to warm-reserve while we investigate. Temporary soft-throttle on tenant egress might keep tail down. Command to apply lightweight fallback (run from router leader):
```
# run on router leader
curl -X POST "http://router-api.local/v1/routing/fallback" -d '{"from_slice":"slice-dedicated-45","to":"warm-reserve-eu1","fraction":0.15}'
```
This should shift ~15% of new allocs off the noisy shelf immediately.
tina: can we do a 5% canary first? steps I propose:
1) apply fraction=0.05
2) watch 99p latency / error rate for 5m
3) if stable, increment to 20% then 50%
Also add a fallback policy that pins requests back if warm-reserve latency > 700ms to avoid oscillation.
aj: agree. also recommend lowering spillback window to 30s to reduce churn while we probe. sample quota tweak for tenant-824 (suspected offender):
```
# tenant egress shaping example
tenant_824:
  egress_bandwidth: 120Mbps
  kvcache_write_burst_limit: 1000/sec
  spillback_window_secs: 30
```
maria: +1. After immediate mitigation, we should tag tenant-824 and run a short isolation test: move that tenant off shelf-17 to a fractional-dedicated carveout for 1h and replay traffic to confirm impact. If noisy pattern repeats, we quarantine automatically after 3 spike events in 24h.
leo: longer term ops note: we should consider adding padding to dedicated slices for the folio workload class during region peaks — +1 or +2 GPUs per hot slice during peak windows. That buys us headroom and reduces emergency shard moves. Estimate monthly cost for eu-west peak padding ~+$5k (we can drive to CFO for budget). Also, please add a SLI for egress queue depth per-shelf to catch this earlier.
infra-bot: [ALERT] 09:34 UTC fallback routing change applied to slice-dedicated-45 by aj. Observed 99p latency down to ~180ms within 90s. Will monitor and autoclose in 15m if stable. (alert-id: alert-2023500002222)
sam: thanks team. I've opened INF-8421 to track mitigation + follow-up. Please paste any telemetry or postmortem notes there. If this repeats tonight we escalate to full PM + SE sync. @oncall-eng-infra FYI :thumbsup:
maria: added telemetry dashboards to INF-8421 — kvcache regen rate, per-tenant egress, host NIC tx_burst, and router fallback ratio. Will run the isolation test in 30m and post results.
aj: rolling canary now (5%). watching.
infra-bot: 09:38 UTC — Canary at 5% shows 99p at 190ms, error rate stable. No new host throttle events.
sam: good. proceed to 20% and keep an eye for oscillation. if warm-reserve sees latency >700ms revert to 0% and raise.
(many short reactions and :thumbsup: on the thread)
